clue.text: Chap offered a lift regularly to Bordeaux, perhaps

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word lift, starting with the first

parts.note: Bordeaux is a French wine, often red, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example of red

explanation.surface: Someone kindly drives a man all the way to Bordeaux.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 1st and 3rd letters of LIFT, giving LF; 'offered' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name stands for any man, which is what the informal word chap means.

clue.text: Writer producing extremely awful chapter — just too much

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters of awful, its first and last

parts.note: OTT stands for over the top, meaning just too much

explanation.surface: A writer turns out a dreadful, overblown chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott was the American novelist who wrote Little Women.

clue.text: Top comedian recoiling in fear?

explanation.surface: The leading comic shrinks back in terror.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is a whimsical title for the best funnyman; as one word it is the verb funk, to flinch from fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A king of fun would be the top comedian; to funk is to shrink back out of fear or cowardice.

clue.text: No longer under pressure to wait around for the milkman?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what one was
P is the physics symbol for pressure
to loiter is to hang about waiting

explanation.surface: Someone no longer pressed to hang about for the milk delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: The milkman here is not a delivery man but one who milks others, taking unfair advantage; 'under' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who milks a person or situation profits selfishly from it, which is what an exploiter does.

clue.text: Teacher and philosopher involved in uncivilised circles

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so the philosopher sits within the other piece
circles means going round and back, so the word for uncivilised is read in reverse

parts.note: rude can mean primitive or uncivilised
Cato was a Roman statesman and Stoic philosopher

explanation.surface: A teacher and a thinker caught up in a boorish crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circles' makes the word for uncivilised go backwards, and 'involved in' puts the Roman thinker inside it; 'circles' looks like a social set but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An educator is someone whose job is instruction, a synonym for a teacher.

clue.text: Distracting account in journal

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the account goes within the journal

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal
a version is one person's account of events

explanation.surface: A diverting story recorded in someone's diary.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversionary move draws attention away, which is to be distracting.

clue.text: It seems like rock song with second and fourth parts transposed

indicators.text: with second and fourth parts transposed
indicators.note: transposed means swapped round, here only the letters in the second and fourth places of the word

parts.note: a carol is a song, especially a Christmas one

explanation.surface: A rock song whose second and fourth sections have been swapped around.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the A and O of CAROL gives the answer; 'rock' looks like a music genre but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is the hard stony skeleton of sea creatures that forms reefs, so it looks like rock without being mineral.

clue.text: Relative's fast speed, going round SW town

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the speed surrounds the relative

parts.note: a ton is slang for 100 mph
an aunt is a relative; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: An aunt speeding at a hundred miles an hour around a town in the south-west.
explanation.walkthrough: TAUNTON is the county town of Somerset in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the county town of Somerset, a town in the south-west of England.

clue.text: Writer beginning to draft sequel to Kidnapped?

parts.note: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter of draft is used

explanation.surface: An author starts drafting a follow-up to Stevenson's novel Kidnapped.
explanation.walkthrough: Kidnapped is Stevenson's novel, but read as a verb what follows being kidnapped is being freed for payment.
explanation.definitionFit: After a kidnapping the usual next event is that the victim is freed on payment of money demanded.

clue.text: A pecan pie as part of a buffet?

indicators.note: pie is printers' jargon for jumbled type, so it signals that the preceding letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A slice of pecan pie served on a buffet table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' looks like the dessert but is the mixing signal applied to A PECAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury on bread or pastry, a typical item laid out at a buffet.

clue.text: Voter wavering near ballot box, upset

indicators.note: wavering means unsteady, so the letters of voter are shaken up

parts.note: an urn is a vessel into which votes may be put

explanation.surface: An undecided voter by the ballot box overturns the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wavering' gives OVERT from VOTER; 'near' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn something is to upset or tip it over.

clue.text: Along with nine others, we stagger about in the dark still

indicators.note: stagger about means reel unsteadily, so the letters of the three words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: We stumble round in the darkness with nine others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stagger about' rearranges the twelve letters of NINE, OTHERS and WE; 'Along with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means knowing no more than before, still uninformed after an explanation.

clue.text: Flag, right one assigned by officer during spell of duty

indicators.note: during means within the period of, so these pieces go inside the spell of duty

parts.note: a tour is a period of duty, as in a tour of duty
I is the Roman numeral one
COL is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: An officer hands out a flag to a man on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assigned by' is a link joining R and I to the colonel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricolour is a national banner of three bands, as in the French one.

clue.text: Printing process that could result in hard toil?

indicators.note: could result in suggests the letters of hard and toil reorganised into a new word

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A printing method that might mean hard labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Litho is short for lithography, a printing technique using a flat stone or plate.

clue.text: Failing tonight, ceased to stay the course

indicators.note: failing means breaking down, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Collapsing tonight, someone stopped before the end of the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' rearranges the letters of TONIGHT and CEASED; the surface of giving up is the opposite of the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to keep going to the very end, especially in a contest.

clue.text: Order to safeguard Pacific island's cultural identity?

indicators.note: to safeguard means to protect by enclosing, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: trim means good order or condition, as in in good trim
Bali is an Indonesian island; the 's supplies an S

explanation.surface: An instruction to protect an island's traditional way of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribalism is strong loyalty to one's own tribe or group, a sense of shared cultural identity.

clue.text: Platform where you'll see 1960s group?

explanation.surface: A stage on which a sixties band performs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scaffold were a 1960s Liverpool comedy and music group known for 'Lily the Pink'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffold is a raised platform, as for an execution, and The Scaffold was a 1960s pop trio.

clue.text: Understanding company's financial provision will protect retired woman

annotationWithheld.why: 'Understanding company's financial provision will protect retired woman': CO + PENSION around REH (retired 'her') gives COPREHENSION; no clue word supplies the M, so the clue as held looks short of a piece.
annotationWithheld.clue: Understanding company's financial provision will protect retired woman

clue.text: Large swimmer worried, being in shock

indicators.note: being in means sitting inside, so the word for worried goes within the shock

parts.note: a shock of hair is a mane
ate is past tense of eat in the sense to worry, as in 'what's eating you'

explanation.surface: A big swimmer was anxious, suffering from shock.
explanation.definitionFit: The manatee or sea cow is a large aquatic mammal.

clue.text: Significant number on board

parts.note: board and table both mean a flat surface for meals, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: An important figure sits on the board of directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is just a link here; 'board' looks like a company's directors but means a table.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means worthy of notice, which is close to important or significant.

clue.text: Cut short useless fruit tree

indicators.note: short means missing its last letter, so the word for cut loses its tail

parts.note: to prune is to cut back
US is short for unserviceable, meaning useless

explanation.surface: A gardener prunes back a fruit tree that bears nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the final E of PRUNE to give PRUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunus is the genus of plum, cherry, peach and almond trees.

clue.text: Discovers diver's beginning to wear flippers

indicators.note: to wear means to have on, so the flippers enclose the letter

parts.note: fins are the rubber flippers divers wear

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of the word diver's

explanation.surface: A diver discovers how to start wearing flippers.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something is to discover it, so finds and discovers are synonyms.

clue.text: What might be sinister at first to sailors?

definitions.text: What might be sinister at first to sailors?

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word sinister

parts.note: RM is the Royal Marines, seagoing soldiers counted as sailors in crosswords

explanation.surface: Asks what seafarers might find ominous from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a gale is something sailors fear.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest at sea is a threat any crew would see as ominous.

clue.text: Someone who shouts out in battle, I'll guarantee

parts.note: a war is a battle on a large scale
a ranter is a person who shouts out wildly

explanation.surface: A soldier bellowing in combat vouches for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll guarantee' is what such a person says of themselves; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One who warrants something gives a formal promise, so the definition is the person's own pledge.

clue.text: Building you once noticed in middle of river

indicators.note: in middle of means placed at the centre of the river's name

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, and another in East Anglia
thou is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A building seen by someone in the middle of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is an English river; 'noticed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An outhouse is a small outbuilding, such as a shed or outdoor toilet.

clue.text: Back view of head on great ape

indicators.note: Back view of means looking from behind, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: nob is slang for head
big means great

explanation.surface: Looking at the back of a gorilla's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back view of' turns the whole run of head-on-great backwards; 'great' seems to belong with 'ape' as in 'great ape' but is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibbon is a small long-armed ape of South-east Asia.

clue.text: Idealists rearmed for revolution, backed by Socialist leader

indicators.note: backed by means supported from behind, so the next piece comes after
for revolution means ready to be overturned, so the letters of rearmed are rearranged
leader means the first letter of the word Socialist

explanation.surface: Rearmed radicals ready for revolt, supported by a left-wing leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for revolution' rearranges the letters of rearmed, and 'backed by' puts the Socialist's initial after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamers are visionaries with impractical ideals, which is what idealists often are.

clue.text: Former ruler's capturing eastern French city

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the ruler's name encloses the letter

parts.note: Idi Amin was the former ruler of Uganda; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A deposed dictator seizes a city in eastern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is a city in northern France, capital of Picardy.
